extractor: read directly from the official GOV.UK pages listed in source_roles
policy: Every entry quotes the official page it was read from. source_excerpt is verbatim government wording, lowercased by the normalizer. Nothing here is paraphrased into a requirement, and nothing is included that the page did not state. The UK publishes no application form identifier for this route, so official_form_code is null everywhere and the online route is recorded as a step.
not_extracted: The registered 'fees' source https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/visa-regulations-revised-table states NO fee amount in its HTML — it is an attachment wrapper listing ODS/HTML fee tables (latest: 'home office immigration and nationality fees, 8 april 2026'; page last updated 18 march 2026). Because it publishes no amount in-page it is absent from source_roles and no requirement cites it. The GBP 558 application fee below is quoted from the registered landing page, which does state it.
The immigration health surcharge amount. The landing page says it is payable and that the amount depends on visa length, but states no figure for this route, so the fee entry below carries no amount.
The amount of money a Student visa applicant must show. GOV.UK puts the maintenance figures on the unregistered sub-page /student-visa/money.
The English language requirement level and how to prove it — unregistered sub-page /student-visa/knowledge-of-english.
Dependant (partner and children) requirements — unregistered sub-page /student-visa/family-members.

Which courses require an ATAS certificate, and which nationalities. GOV.UK links out to a separate ATAS service; the documents page only says a certificate is needed 'if your course and nationality require it'.
The list of licensed student sponsors, and the list of countries whose nationals must take a tuberculosis test. Both are separate GOV.UK services, not registered sources.
Priority / faster-decision service fees — mentioned but with no amount stated on any registered page.

requirements.label: Study a course eligible for the Student visa
requirements.description: GOV.UK lists: a full-time course below degree level (RQF level 3, 4 or 5) with at least 15 hours a week of organised daytime study; a full-time course at degree level or above (RQF level 6, 7 or 8); a full-time degree-level course equivalent to a UK higher education course delivered as part of a longer overseas course; a part-time course above degree level (RQF level 7 or above); an English language course at CEFR level B2 or above. A full-time elected student union sabbatical officer post also qualifies. Qualification levels differ in Scotland.
requirements.source_excerpt: you can do one of the following courses: a full-time course leading to a qualification that’s below degree level ( rqf level 3, 4 or 5) with at least 15 hours a week of organised daytime study
requirements.source_excerpt_display: You can do one of the following courses: a full-time course leading to a qualification that’s below degree level (RQF level 3, 4 or 5) with at least 15 hours a week of organised daytime study

requirements.description: GOV.UK gives a different window for applications made inside the UK: the earliest is 3 months before the course starts, you must apply before your current visa expires, and the new course must begin within 28 days of that expiry.

requirements.source_excerpt_display: Applying from outside the UK The earliest you can apply for a visa is 6 months before you start your course.

requirements.label: Apply online for the Student visa
requirements.description: The UK publishes no application form number for this route — the application exists only as an online service. GOV.UK states you can save the form and complete it later.
requirements.source_excerpt: you must apply online for a student visa.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: You must apply online for a Student visa.

requirements.label: Prove your identity, by app or at a visa application centre
requirements.description: GOV.UK states you will either use the 'UK Immigration: ID Check' app to scan your identity document (creating or signing into a UKVI account), or have your fingerprints and photo taken at a visa application centre. Which one applies depends on where you are from and what type of passport you have; you are told when you apply. If you need an appointment you must take your passport, and the centre may be in another country.
requirements.source_excerpt: as part of your application, you’ll need to prove your identity. how you do this depends on where you’re from and what type of passport you have.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: As part of your application, you’ll need to prove your identity. How you do this depends on where you’re from and what type of passport you have.

requirements.label: Student visa application fee
requirements.description: GBP 558 whether you apply from outside the UK or extend or switch from inside the UK. The fee is payable for each person that joins you.

requirements.source_excerpt: it costs: £558 to apply for a student visa from outside the uk ... £558 to extend or switch to a student visa from inside the uk ... you must pay the visa fee for each person that joins you.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: It costs: £558 to apply for a Student visa from outside the UK ... £558 to extend or switch to a Student visa from inside the UK ... You must pay the visa fee for each person that joins you.
